dedupe_keys.name: earthquake risk assessment framework for container port systems georgia tech nees grand challenge

description: This framework assesses earthquake risk for a container port as a system of berths, not for single structures. The authors, from the Georgia Institute of Technology, note that seismic risk practice in ports considered only the performance of individual wharf and crane structures, not how their damage and downtime disrupt port-wide ship handling or the regional, national and international economic impacts of a long disruption at a major container port; West Coast earthquakes are the motivating concern. The work was part of a Grand Challenge project of the National Science Foundation Network for Earthquake Engineering Simulation. The paper gives an overview of the concepts and methods for seismic risk assessment of a port-wide system of berths with their wharf and crane structures, and examples of how port decision makers could use the analysis to choose among design, retrofit, operational and other seismic risk management options. Access: Transportation Research Record 2166 (2010). Licence and cost: subscription. Caveats: only the abstract was read; no software release is named. It supports hazard exposure, resilience and capacity planning models of ports. It relates to the SimPy container terminal model, global port risk data and the Port of Mobile hurricane case in the catalogue.
